newsitem.title: GERMANY: Leader of German Jewish youth fears for the future.
newsitem.headline: Leader of German Jewish youth fears for the future.

text.p: The leader of a German Jewish youth organisation said on Thurday he hoped a Berlin conference for teenagers would help resuscitate the fight for the future survival of an active German Jewish community.
"We have little leadership power in our community right now," Jeffrey Drimmer, chairman of the B'nai B'rith Youth Organisation (BBYO) in Germany, told Reuters.
"We need to develop this group of young people to create that (leadership base) for the next generation," Drimmer said.

Under the banner "Unite & ACT" the BBYO will launch its third annual week-long meeting in Berlin on Saturday, bringing 80 teenagers from nine countries to discuss fighting racism and anti-Semitism in their communities.
BBYO is the world's largest Jewish youth organisation with 20,000 members.

Its five-year old German chapter, set up during a three-year upsurge of racist violence after unification in 1990, has between 100 and 200 active participants among a Jewish community of around 50,000.
"Anti-semitism and racism have gotten much worse since the Berlin Wall fell," Drimmer said. "You suddenly had 16 million East Germans who didn't know what Jews were, joining the rest of Germany."
Drimmer cited a rise in attacks on Jewish cultural centres and memorials and violence against Jews since unification.
"The idea behind this program is to get young people out of their communities and working to create a better Europe by fighting racism and anti-Semitism," he said.

This year's Unite & ACT program will also feature dialogue between religions including discussions between Buddhists, Moslems, Christians and Jews from across western and eastern Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia.
